title: Eating Through Mexico City in One Day
creator: Mara Quintero
description:
Tacos al pastor, tamales at dawn, mole in Coyoacán and churros at midnight. One day, way too much food.

Travel insurance from Trailpass, our sponsor: get a quote at https://trailpass.com/mara

All the places we ate are pinned in the comments.

sentences.t: It's seven in the morning in Mexico City and I'm already eating, which is how you know it's going to be a good day.
This is a tamale from a lady with a cart outside the metro, and it's wrapped in a corn husk and stuffed with green salsa and chicken.
And you can get it inside a bread roll, which is called a guajolota, which is a tamale sandwich, which is genius.
Today the plan is simple, eat as much as humanly possible in one day.
But first, we've got two sponsors to thank for this trip, so bear with me.
The first one is Trailpass, the travel insurance I use for every single trip now.
Last year in Peru I got food poisoning so bad I ended up in a clinic, and Trailpass covered the whole thing, and I filed the claim from my phone in the waiting room.
They cover medical stuff, cancelled flights, and lost bags, and you can buy a policy even after you've already left home.
Get a quote in about two minutes at trailpass.com/mara.
Our second sponsor is Kettle and Crane, and this one is very on theme, because it's coffee.
They work directly with small farms, including a few here in Mexico, and they roast to order and ship it to you within days.
You pick how much you drink and how often, and you can pause or skip a delivery whenever you want.
Use code MARA for your first bag free at kettleandcrane.com.
Okay, mid morning stop, and we're in the Roma neighborhood for chilaquiles.
That's fried tortilla chips simmered in salsa, so they're soft and crunchy at the same time, with a fried egg and crema on top.
I went for the red salsa, and it's smoky and a little bit spicy, and I could eat this every morning forever.
Next, a market in the center, where we wander the stalls and try a little of everything.
Fresh mango with chili and lime, a cup of jícama, and a sip of a green juice the lady promised me was healthy.
Lunch is the main event, and we're heading to Coyoacán for mole.
This is mole negro, made with something like thirty ingredients, including chilies, chocolate, nuts, and spices.
It takes days to make, and you can taste every hour of it.
It's rich, it's slightly bitter, slightly sweet, and it's poured over chicken with rice on the side.
I need a nap, but there is no time for a nap.
Afternoon, we walk it off around the plaza and get an ice cream, because walking it off counts even if you eat while doing it.
Then evening, which means tacos al pastor.
This is the spot everyone told me about, a tiny stand with a giant spinning cone of marinated pork and a pineapple on top.
The guy slices the pork right onto the tortilla, flicks a piece of pineapple on top, and it lands perfectly every single time.
I watched him do it twenty times and he never missed once.
Onion, cilantro, green salsa, a squeeze of lime, and done.
I had five, and I regret nothing.
And to finish the night, it's almost midnight and we're at a churrería that's been open since nineteen thirty five.
Fresh churros, still hot, dipped in thick hot chocolate.
This is the perfect ending to a ridiculous day of eating.
Total damage for the whole day was about seven hundred pesos for two people, so around forty dollars.
Mexico City, you are incredible, and I'm coming back very soon.
Let me know your favorite dish here in the comments, and I'll see you in the next video.
